eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Measurable or evaluable disease
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: have either measurable or evaluable disease using standard techniques by the Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors, Version 1.1 (RECIST 1.1) (Eisenhauer et al. 2009).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Informed consent and authorization
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: The patient, or patient's parent/guardian, has given written informed consent (and assent, as applicable) and authorization for release of health/information for research prior to any study_specific procedures being performed (refer to Appendix 2, Study Governance, Regulatory, and Ethical Considerations).

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Performance score requirement
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: The patient has a Lansky (<16 years of age; Lansky et al. 1987) or Karnofsky (≥16 years of age; Karnofsky et al. 1948) performance score of at least 50.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Discontinuation of previous treatments
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: Patients must have discontinued all previous treatments for cancer or investigational agents ≥7 days after the last dose or as shown below, and must have recovered from the acute effects to ≤Grade 2 for alopecia and decreased tendon reflex and to ≤Grade 1 for all other effects at the time of enrollment, unless otherwise noted. For agents with known AEs occurring beyond the required wait period outlined in the table, this period must be extended until after the time during which the AE is known to occur. Consult with the Lilly CRS/CRP for the appropriate length of time prior to the first dose of study treatment on additional therapies not mentioned. Previous treatments and required wait periods: Cytotoxic and myelosuppressive chemotherapy: ≥14 days after the last dose of cytotoxic or myelosuppressive chemotherapy (or ≥42 days if prior nitrosourea); Hematopoietic growth factors: ≥14 days after the last dose of a long_acting growth factor (for example, pegfilgrastim) or ≥48 hours for short_acting growth factor; Cellular therapy: ≥42 days after the completion of any type of cellular therapy (eg modified T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells, etc.) agent; Interleukins, interferons, and cytokines (other than hematopoietic growth factors): ≥21 days after the completion of interleukins, interferon, or cytokines (other than hematopoietic growth factors); Antibody therapy: ≥21 days after the last infusion of antibody therapy; Radiotherapy: ≥14 days since local palliative radiation therapy (RT) (small port); craniospinal XRT, or 50% or greater pelvic radiation; ≥42 days for other substantial radiation (such as metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy); Radiopharmaceutical therapy (eg, radiolabeled antibody, 131I_MIBG): ≥42 days after systemically administered radiopharmaceutical therapy; Stem cell infusion without TBI: ≥84 days must have elapsed after auto_transplant or stem cell infusion; Corticosteroids: ≥14 days for patients who have received a course of systemic corticosteroids (≥5 days) to modify immune AEs related to prior therapy. Note: Patients who are on chronic replacement dose for endocrine disorders or are on a stable or decreasing dose for indications other than treating the underlying cancer, may still be eligible (consult Lilly CRP/CRS); Live vaccines: ≥28 days after last live vaccine.

eligibilityCriterionItems.name: Adequate hematologic and organ function
eligibilityCriterionItems.text: The patient has adequate hematologic and organ function ≤1 week (7 days) prior to first dose of study drug.

arms.name: To be defined per addendum
arms.description: Each addendum defines its own treatment arms, including investigational drug(s) alone or in combination with other treatments. Specific arm details, doses, and durations are provided in each protocol addendum.

arms.name: Control Arm (shared or addendum_specific)
arms.description: A common control arm may be shared across addenda of common scientific interest to minimize the number of patients exposed to potentially less effective therapies. Specific control arm details are defined in each addendum.

objectives.name: Master Protocol Framework Objective
objectives.text: The main purpose of the CAMPFIRE Master Protocol is to create a framework to seamlessly evaluate the efficacy and safety of each investigational agent or study drug regimen eligible for development in specified populations of pediatric and young adult patients.

endpoints.name: Investigation_Specific Endpoints
endpoints.text: The clinical research objectives and endpoints for specific investigations are detailed in each individual addendum.

estimands.name: Investigation_Specific Efficacy Estimand (Master Protocol Framework)
estimands.populationSummary: Pediatric and young adult patients with cancer meeting investigation_specific eligibility criteria as defined in each individual addendum (Investigation_specific analysis population as defined in each addendum (e.g., Intent_to_Treat or modified Intent_to_Treat population)) Summary measure: Investigation_specific summary measure as defined in each addendum statistical analysis plan (e.g., objective response rate, hazard ratio, difference in means).

intercurrentEvents.name: Discontinuation of study treatment
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient discontinues investigational study treatment prior to the planned end of treatment as defined in the addendum, due to adverse events, disease progression, withdrawal of consent, or investigator decision

intercurrentEvents.name: Use of prohibited concomitant therapy
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient initiates prohibited or restricted concomitant therapy as specified in the addendum_specific list of restricted and prohibited concomitant therapies

intercurrentEvents.name: Death
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient dies prior to the planned efficacy assessment timepoint as defined in the addendum

intercurrentEvents.name: Disease progression requiring alternative therapy
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient experiences disease progression and initiates alternative anticancer therapy outside of the study treatment regimen prior to the planned efficacy assessment

intercurrentEvents.name: Dose modification
intercurrentEvents.text: Patient undergoes dose reduction or dose interruption of the investigational agent as specified in the addendum_specific dose modification guidelines

notes.text: Note to Regulatory Authorities: This document may contain protected personal data and/or commercially confidential information exempt from public disclosure. Eli Lilly and Company requests consultation regarding release/redaction prior to any public release. In the United States, this document is subject to Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) Exemption 4 and may not be reproduced or otherwise disseminated without the written approval of Eli Lilly and Company or its subsidiaries.
Prospective approval of protocol deviations to recruitment and enrollment criteria, also known as protocol waivers or exemptions, is not permitted.

G_CSF permitted up to 48 hours prior. Patients with documented history of benign ethnic neutropenia or other conditions could be considered with a lower ANC after discussion with and approval from the Lilly CRP/CRS.
Platelet transfusion permitted up to 72 hours prior.

Transfusions to increase the patient's hemoglobin level to at least 8 g/dL are permitted; however, study treatment must not begin until 7 days after the transfusion, and CBC criteria for eligibility are confirmed within 24 hr of C1D1.
Except patients with documented history of Gilbert Syndrome who must have a total bilirubin level of <3.0×ULN.
Abbreviations: ALT = alanine aminotransferase; ANC = absolute neutrophil count; AST = aspartate aminotransferase; CBC = complete blood count; ULN = upper limit of normal.
The threshold creatinine values in this table were derived from the Schwartz formula for estimating glomerular filtration rate (Appendix 4).
Consult with the Lilly CRS/CRP for the appropriate length of time prior to the first dose of study treatment on additional therapies not mentioned.
For agents with known AEs occurring beyond the required wait period outlined in the table, this period must be extended until after the time during which the AE is known to occur.

A patient will be considered significantly noncompliant if he or she is judged by the investigator to have intentionally or repeatedly taken more or less than the prescribed amount of medication. The threshold required to maintain status as compliant will be at least 80% unless otherwise specified in Section 3.6.5 of the specifically enrolled addendum.

Investigators are not obligated to actively seek AEs or SAEs in patients once they have discontinued and/or completed the study (the patient summary CRF has been completed). However, if the investigator learns of any SAE, including a death, at any time after a patient has been discharged from the study, and he/she considers the event reasonably possibly related to the study treatment or study participation, the investigator must promptly notify Lilly.

Planned hospitalizations or procedures for preexisting conditions that were recorded in the patient's medical history at the time of enrollment should not be considered SAEs. Hospitalization or prolongation of hospitalization without a precipitating clinical AE (for example, for the administration of study treatment or other protocol_required procedure) should not be considered SAEs.
Serious adverse events, including death, caused by disease progression should not be reported unless the investigator deems them to be possibly related to study treatment.
Bioanalytical samples collected to measure study drug concentration will be retained for a maximum of 1 year following the last patient visit for the study.

A legal representative must give informed consent for a child to participate in this study. In addition to informed consent given by the legal representative, the child may be required to give documented assent, if capable.
The ERB/IRB should include or consult with experts who are knowledgeable in pediatric ethical, clinical, and psychosocial issues.

Participating in one investigation does not preclude the patient from enrolling in another investigation within the CAMPFIRE Master Protocol at a subsequent time as long as eligibility criteria are met.

studyInterventions.name: Lilly investigational drug(s)
studyInterventions.description: Eli Lilly and Company investigational drugs evaluated alone or in combination with various treatments in pediatric and young adult patients with cancer. Specific agents are defined in individual protocol addenda.

studyInterventions.name: Combination agents / comparator treatments
studyInterventions.description: Various available treatments or other investigational agents used in combination with or as comparators to Lilly investigational drugs. Specific comparators are defined in individual protocol addenda. Common control arms may be shared across addenda.

studyInterventions.name: Concomitant supportive care medications
studyInterventions.description: Permitted supportive care therapies including sedatives, antibiotics, analgesics, antihistamines, corticosteroids (chronic replacement dose or stable/decreasing dose for non_cancer indications), erythropoietin, blood products (blood cells, platelets, fresh frozen plasma transfusions), and procedures such as paracentesis and thoracentesis. All must be documented on eCRF.

studyInterventions.name: Hematopoietic growth factors
studyInterventions.description: G_CSF and other hematopoietic growth factors permitted up to 48 hours (short_acting) or 14 days (long_acting, e.g., pegfilgrastim) prior to first dose of study treatment. Also permitted during study as supportive care.

studyInterventions.name: Platelet transfusions
studyInterventions.description: Platelet transfusions permitted up to 72 hours prior to first dose to meet eligibility criteria (platelets ≥75,000/mm3).

studyInterventions.name: Red blood cell transfusions
studyInterventions.description: Transfusions permitted to increase hemoglobin to at least 8 g/dL for eligibility; study treatment must not begin until 7 days after transfusion and CBC criteria confirmed within 24 hours of C1D1.

studyInterventions.name: Chemotherapy (cytotoxic and myelosuppressive)
studyInterventions.description: Must be discontinued ≥14 days before first dose of study treatment (≥42 days if prior nitrosourea). Patient must have recovered from acute effects.

studyInterventions.name: Cellular therapy
studyInterventions.description: Modified T cells, NK cells, dendritic cells, etc. must be discontinued ≥42 days before first dose of study treatment.

studyInterventions.name: Interleukins, interferons, and cytokines
studyInterventions.description: Must be discontinued ≥21 days before first dose of study treatment (excluding hematopoietic growth factors).

studyInterventions.name: Antibody therapy
studyInterventions.description: Must be discontinued ≥21 days (last infusion) before first dose of study treatment.

studyInterventions.name: Radiotherapy
studyInterventions.description: Local palliative RT (small port): ≥14 days; craniospinal XRT or ≥50% pelvic radiation: ≥14 days; other substantial radiation (e.g., metaiodobenzylguanidine therapy): ≥42 days before first dose of study treatment.

studyInterventions.name: Radiopharmaceutical therapy
studyInterventions.description: Systemically administered radiopharmaceutical therapy (e.g., radiolabeled antibody, 131I_MIBG) must be discontinued ≥42 days before first dose of study treatment.

studyInterventions.name: Stem cell infusion (without TBI)
studyInterventions.description: Auto_transplant or stem cell infusion must have occurred ≥84 days before first dose of study treatment.

studyInterventions.name: Systemic corticosteroids
studyInterventions.description: Patients who received a course of systemic corticosteroids (≥5 days) to modify immune AEs related to prior therapy must have discontinued ≥14 days before first dose. Patients on chronic replacement dose for endocrine disorders or stable/decreasing dose for non_cancer indications may still be eligible.

studyInterventions.name: Live vaccines
studyInterventions.description: Must be discontinued ≥28 days before first dose of study treatment.

studyInterventions.name: Other chemotherapy, investigational medications, anticancer therapy, immunotherapy, hormonal cancer therapy
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited while patients are on study treatment. No other chemotherapy, investigational medications, other anticancer therapy, immunotherapy, hormonal cancer therapy, palliative radiation, or palliative surgery for cancer permitted during study treatment. Exceptions defined in each addendum.
